cues.text: Good morning. You’re through to the tourist information office, Tim speaking. How can I help you?
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Oh hello. Could you give me some information about next month’s festival, please? My family and I will be staying in the town that week.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Of course. Well it starts with a concert on the afternoon of the 17th.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Oh I heard about that. The orchestra and singers come from the USA, don’t they?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: They’re from Canada. They’re very popular over there. They’re going to perform a number of well-known pieces that will appeal to children as well as adults.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: That sounds good. My whole family are interested in music.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: The next day, the 18th, there’s a performance by a ballet company called Eustatis.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Sorry?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: The name is spelt E-U-S-T-A-T-I-S. They appeared in last year’s festival, and went down very well. Again, their programme is designed for all ages.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Good. I expect we’ll go to that. I hope there’s going to be a play during the festival, a comedy, ideally.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: You’re in luck! On the 19th and 20th a local amateur group are performing one written by a member of group. It’s called Jemima. That’ll be on in the town hall. They’ve already performed it two or three times. I haven’t seen it myself, but the review in the local paper was very good.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: And is it suitable for children?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Yes, in fact it’s aimed more at children than at adults, so both performances are in the afternoon.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: And what about dance ? Will there by any performances?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Yes, also on the 20th, but in the evening. A professional company is putting on a show of modern pieces, with electronic music by young composers.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Uh-huh.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: The show is about how people communicate, or fail to communicate, with each other, so it’s got the rather strange name, Chat.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: I suppose that’s because that’s something we do both face to face and online.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: That’s right.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Now there are also some workshops and other activities. They’ll all take place at least once every day, so everyone who wants to take part will have a chance.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Good. We’re particularly interested in cookery – you don’t happen to have a cookery workshop, do you?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: We certainly do. It’s going to focus on how to make food part of a healthy lifestyle, and it’ll show that even sweet things like cakes can contain much less sugar than they usually do.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: That might be worth going to. We’re trying to encourage our children to cook.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Another workshop is just for children, and that’s on creating posters to reflect the history of the town. The aim is to make children aware of how both the town and people’s lives have changed over the centuries.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: The results will be exhibited in the community centre. Then the other workshop is in toy-making, and that’s for adults only.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Oh, why’s that?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Because it involves carpentry – participants will be making toys out of wood, so there’ll be a lot of sharp chisels and other tools around.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: It makes sense to keep children away from it.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Exactly. Now let me tell you about some of the outdoor activities. There’ll be supervised wild swimming …
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Wild swimming? What’s that?
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: It just means swimming in natural waters, rather than a swimming pool.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Oh OK. In a lake, for instance.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: Yes, there’s a beautiful one just outside the town, and that’ll be the venue for the swimming. There’ll be lifeguards on duty, so it’s suitable for all ages. And finally, there’ll be a walk in some nearby woods every day.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: The leader is an expert on insects. He’ll show some that live in the woods, and how important they are for the environment. So there are going to be all sorts of different things to do during the festival.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: There certainly are.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: If you’d like to read about how the preparations for the festival are going, the festival organizer is keeping a blog. Just search online for the festival website, and you’ll find it.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Well, thank you very much for all the information.
cues.speaker: JEAN

cues.text: You’re welcome. Goodbye.
cues.speaker: TIM

cues.text: Goodbye.
cues.speaker: JEAN
